text:
sofia: heads up — evening slice change window starts at 20:00 PT (30m). quick rollcall and sanity checklist?

mike: i'm on. canary deploys prepped. pinned model-serving image to rwinf/model:release-2026-03-21-rc1

jordan: oncall here. perf dashboards look OK. i'll set alert thresholds to 2x baseline for the first 15m and watch error budget

deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated -> service: inference-ded-cc-2, version: release-2026-03-21-rc1, config: batch_size=8, kvcache=enabled

sofia: smoke criteria: 95th latency < 120ms, error-rate < 0.2%, embeddings throughput within 10% of baseline. if any fail, immediate pause and triage

lee: running quick smoke locally now — using the lightweight harness to hit canary:
```bash
./scripts/smoke.sh --target inference-ded-cc-2 --qps 15 --duration 60
```

deploy-bot: canary progress 25% -> 3/12 hosts updated, no runtime errors reported yet

mike: seeing a small transient spike in token-cost metric but it's within the expected approximation window. logging it but not blocking

jordan: noticed a transient 503 on canary host 3, checking logs and network health

lee: log snippet from host3:
```
ERROR: grpc: connection reset by peer
stack: kvcache.go:124
meta: active-kv-size=4.2GB
```

mike: if it repeats and error-rate > 0.5% over a 5m window we rollback. rollback command (ops playbook):
`deploy rollback --service inference-ded-cc-2 --to release-2026-03-20-stable --reason "canary error spike"`

sofia: decision: continue canary for now, ops-oncall you own rollback authority. if alerts hit thresholds we execute the rollback command and notify #release-war-room

ops-oncall: acknowledged — watching alerts and metrics dashboards. will run the rollback if >0.5% errors or 2x latency breach sustained for 10m

deploy-bot: canary progress 75% -> 9/12 hosts updated, no sustained errors

sofia: release-note (short): runtime kernel optimizations for long-context inference; expected p99 improvement and ~6% cost reduction. no model or API surface changes.

jordan: errors dropped back to 0.1% and latency within smoke criteria. continuing to monitor for 20 more minutes before full rollout

mike: tagging release in release notes: "runtime-kernel-optimizations — cost ~6%" @release-team. reminded folks to watch billing alerts for next 24h

sofia: thank you everyone. if we need to post-action anything we'll open a follow-up thread. closing watch after full rollout completes :thumbsup:
